summary.text: A 38-month-old girl with Goldenhar syndrome diagnosed as a newborn was born at term after a normal pregnancy. Postnatally she had nasal obstruction, inspiratory dyspnea, feeding difficulties, vomiting, apnea and cyanosis. Bilateral choanal atresia was identified and treated with surgical lysis and stent mounting. She also had microretrognathism, microcrania, mandibular hypoplasia, low ear implantation, pre-auricular appendix, short neck and bilateral microtia.

Brain CT at 23 months showed cleft palate, adenoid hyperplasia with partial choanal atresia, left EAC atresia, right EAC stenosis, an unidentified left ossicle chain apart from part of the hammer, and normal internal auditory canal morphology. At 11 months moderate conductive/mixed hearing loss in the right ear and severe mixed hearing loss in the left ear were diagnosed; the audiologic profile is tabulated.

Hearing rehabilitation used the BAHA Softband. At 38 months the control audiogram showed 30 dB HL thresholds in the sound field, and P1 CAEP after 27 months of hearing aid use showed normal latency (125 ms) and morphology with amplitude 3.31 μV. The authors interpret this as suggestive of normal central auditory pathway development and recommend CAEP reevaluation.

DDST II was first performed at 32 months and repeated at 38 months after integration into a rehabilitation program with physical therapy, speech therapy and auditory-verbal stimulation. Conventional scoring was suspect at both ages; adapted scores rose in all four areas, and the developmental quotient was lower than 1. Language and personal-social estimates were lowest, and motor delays and overall progress were reported to improve after therapy.
